confirmed.title: Accountant can close any member's account
confirmed.rootCause: canSee() widens the ownership check to admit any 'accountant', but that widened check is baked into getOwnAccount(), which every account route reuses as its sole authorization gate — including POST /accounts/:id/close (mutates state) and POST /accounts/:id/export (writes a CSV side effect) — so an accountant, who the PR's own contract says 'cannot deposit or otherwise change state'/'changes nothing', can actually close or export any other user's account; the new test only exercises the two genuinely read-only routes (GET account, GET transfers) and never close or export, so it passes despite the hole. Verified empirically in the worktree: with role 'accountant' and no ownership, POST /accounts/:id/close returned 200 with closed:true on another user's account, and POST /accounts/:id/export returned 200 and ran the export for another user's account.
confirmed.summary: canSee()'s role-only widening is applied inside getOwnAccount, which closeAccount() reuses as its authorization gate, so an accountant — who the PR says 'cannot deposit or otherwise change state' — can actually close any other user's zero-balance account via POST /accounts/:id/close.
confirmed.failure: Given a member Bob who opens account A (balance 0) and an accountant Eve (role 'accountant', not the owner), calling POST /accounts/A/close with Eve's token returns 200 with {closed:true}: the account is mutated (closedAt set, recorded in the audit log as Eve's action) even though Eve owns neither the account nor an admin role. I verified this directly: ran a POC request through the real server/store (freshStore + serve from test/helpers.js) — POST /accounts/<bobsAccount>/close with an accountant token returned status 200 and closed:true, i.e. the account was actually closed by a non-owning, non-admin accountant. There is no reopen endpoint in src/server.js, so this is an irreversible state change caused entirely by a role the PR describes as read-only. The root cause is that closeAccount(store, user, id) (src/accounts.js:48-55) calls getOwnAccount for its ownership check, and getOwnAccount now accepts any accountant via canSee's `|| user.role === 'accountant'` branch (src/accounts.js:38-40) — a check that was written for read access but is shared, unmodified, by a mutating code path. The same reuse also lets an accountant trigger POST /accounts/:id/export (src/server.js:97-105), writing a CSV file to disk for any account, which likewise isn't a pure read. The new test added in this diff (test/server.test.js, 'an accountant reads any account and its transfers') only exercises the two safe read routes and does not touch /close or /export, so it does not catch this.

confirmed.reasoning: Read src/accounts.js: getOwnAccount (line 42-46) now gates on canSee(user, account), which returns true for any user.role === 'accountant' regardless of ownership. closeAccount (line 48-55) calls getOwnAccount as its sole authorization check, then mutates state (store.update closedAt) and records an audit entry under the accountant's own user.id if balanceCents === 0. In src/server.js, both POST /accounts/:id/close (line 62-70) and POST /accounts/:id/export (line 97-105) are wrapped only in requireUser (no requireRole/ownership check beyond getOwnAccount) and call getOwnAccount directly. requireUser (src/auth.js) only authenticates a token into a user; it enforces no role or ownership restriction itself. I reproduced this empirically in the worktree using the existing test/helpers.js (freshStore + serve): inserted an 'accountant' user Eve, had member Bob open a zero-balance account, then called POST /accounts/<bob's id>/close with Eve's token -> HTTP 200, body {..., closed: true}, i.e. Bob's account was actually closed by a non-owning, non-admin accountant. I then called POST /accounts/<bob's id>/export with Eve's token -> HTTP 200 {exported: 0}, and confirmed the CSV file was actually written to disk at <tmpdir>/exports/<account id>.csv (existsSync returned true). There is no reopen endpoint in src/server.js or README.md (grepped, none found), so the close is irreversible via the API. The PR's own new test (test/server.test.js, 'an accountant reads any account and its transfers') only calls GET /accounts/:id and GET /accounts/:id/transfers for the accountant, never /close or /export, so this hole is untested and passes CI. This fully matches the claim's mechanism, affected routes, and non-detection by the new test.
confirmed.panel: 3 of 3 skeptics could not refute it

missed.what: The export route (POST /accounts/:id/export, src/server.js:101) also calls the now-widened getOwnAccount, so an accountant can force a CSV write to disk for any account they don't own. Verified live: an accountant token triggered export on another user's account, got HTTP 200, and a real file landed at exports/<accountId>.csv. This is a second mutation-adjacent path (filesystem write) reusing the same widened check -- distinct from the already-flagged account-close bug -- letting the new lower-trust role write files for arbitrary accounts, directly contradicting the PR's own stated intent that an accountant 'cannot deposit or otherwise change state.'
missed.why: The scout's state-change-via-read-path angle scanned this exact root cause but its reported finding names only closeAccount (accounts.js:49), not server.js's export route, which is a different file/line with a different consequence (disk I/O for accounts the accountant doesn't own, landing in a shared export directory) that the given finding does not cover. It falls in the gap between 'this angle ran' and 'this angle followed every caller of the changed helper.'

missed.what: The feature's own stated purpose -- 'an accountant may read any account' for reconciliation -- has no discovery path: GET /accounts (listAccounts) still filters strictly by ownerId === user.id, unchanged by this PR. Verified live: an accountant with zero accounts of her own gets {total: 0} from GET /accounts even though another user's account exists. So an accountant can only ever reach an account via GET /accounts/:id if they already know its id out-of-band; there is no route that lets them enumerate or browse the ledger they're meant to reconcile.
missed.why: No angle in the list targets feature completeness against the PR's own description -- correctness and boundary-contract check that existing logic behaves correctly on its stated inputs, not that a promised capability (browsing 'any account') is actually reachable through any route. The single new test only exercises a hand-fed account id, so tests-that-dont-test had no hollow assertion to catch here; the gap is an entire missing endpoint, not a wrong one.
